# The Stone Snakes

*Pages PDF 52-61*

## ## the Stone Snakes
## **Waaagh! Against the Machines**
The Stone Snakes are a band of Savage Orcs who have rejected Orc civilisation, eschewing metalworking, limiting themselves to artefacts of stone, animal hide, and wood. Savage Orcs consider themselves blessed for this, although their aversion to modernity might help explain why the Stone Snakes tribe was captured and enslaved by Chaos Dwarfs in the Darklands. From the perspective of their shaman and chief, however, it was all a part of Mork’s plan. 

Following a severe beating by a Chaos Dwarf overseer, the Stone Snake’s apprentice Shaman (his master previously flattened by a spiked steamroller) experienced a divine revelation. During a violent thunderstorm, Hizsss Snakeskin had a vision of Mork, who told him to free his tribe. 

When Hizsss complained that the enemy were too many, Mork said, “Release da Humies! Dere’s loads of ‘em down ‘ere wiv us! Get ‘em to work for us!“ Hizsss received a vision in which he was struck by a bolt of green lightning and imbued with great power. 

Freeing his tribe from their shackles with magic, he gave a young Orc named Bruug the following order: “Go! Find an’ ‘ammer and giv it to an ‘Umie.” 

Bruug bravely followed the order, waking an Ungol chieftain who had been kept captive alongside the Orcs, giving him a mallet and chisel to break his chains: “We’z all breakin’ out! You get yor lot to go left and we’ll go…” Bruug looked at his hands, “we’ll go… da uvver way!” Thunder bursts covered the sound of hammering, but even the tempest wasn’t loud enough to cover the screams of Chaos Dwarfs and Hobgoblins in the resulting slaughter. 

Before the battle was quite over, Hizsss gave the order to run for it. He wasn’t waiting to see how the freed Human captives were going to react and after their mistreatment by the Chaos Dwarfs his tribe wasn’t up to taking on a load of Ungols who’d got their dander up. 

Since then, Hizsss and the Stone Snakes have made it their mission to harass Chaos Dwarfs, break their machines, free their captives. It’s a stealthy guerrilla war and probably unwinnable, but when has that ever stopped an Orc? 

## **Disposition of the Stone Snakes**
The Stone Snakes are nomadic but rarely travel together. Instead, they go forth in small groups, taking separate, circuitous routes, coming together at agreed meeting points. At the start of the journey, there are perhaps three to six Orcs per group. As they get closer to the rendezvous, they start coming together, forming bands of half a dozen, a dozen, and so on, until the tribe is together again. At full strength, the tribe consists of the following: 

- Hizsss Snakeskin and Slith Snake-Wrangla in the company of a couple of Savage Orc Elites (acting as bodyguards), and a couple of Savage Orc Skirmishers (as scouts and lookouts). 

- Up to ten units of three to six Savage Orcs, including at least one Elite, one Soldier, and one Skirmisher. 

- Bruug, working as an auxillary, often in the role of an outrider (albeit one who travels on foot) for one of the units mentioned above. 

- Up to twenty units of a single Skirmisher, such as Garn, working as a solo operative, often far from other members of the tribe, gathering information on enemy movements, or acting in the role of a saboteur and assassin. This force may coalesce into a single fighting unit if the situation calls for it. 

## **Uniform**
Stone Snakes wear garments stitched from animal skins, commonly from large snakes, but also other monstrous Dark Lands beasts. Dried snake’s heads and fangs are common ornamentation, but there is no other uniformity. 

## We’d Look into It Ourselves, but...
Dwarf scouts from the mountains who cautiously keep an eye on Chaos Dwarf activity have become aware of an unknown group acting against the enemy, releasing slaves, attacking supply wagons, and smashing their diabolical machinery. They’ve heard rumours of Dwarf captives being freed, but finding Dwarfs willing to talk about their experiences has proved impossible, as though something shameful happened. Causing trouble for Chaos Dwarfs is always a good thing, but the Dwarfs are concerned about an unknown third party and what their ultimate goal is. Also, the release of slaves from different races and tribes could shift the power dynamic in the Dark Lands, especially if a single powerful leader arises among them. The Dwarfs may well be willing to recruit the Characters for an investigative excursion into the Dark Lands. 

## A Crude Awakening
Should the Characters ever become unwilling guests of the Chaos Dwarfs, they may experience emancipation at the hands of the Stone Snakes. One of the Characters is woken in the middle of the Dark Land’s thunderstorms. Exhausted from the day’s slaving, it’s not the thunder that wakes them, but a oneeyed Orc they’ve never met before. He gives them a hammer and chisel, “We’z bustin’ you out!” Then he vanishes. Assuming the Character takes up the offer, the thunder covers the sound of hammering. Once hands and feet are free of chains, the Characters hear the first screams. The place is in chaos, as prisoners from different species free themselves and lay into the Chaos Dwarfs and their allies. In the frenzy, the Characters spot their liberator in need of help. 

## **Equipment**
Stone Snakes fashion weapons from natural materials: snake fangs, flint or obsidian daggers, stone hammers, clubs, and slings. 

## **Shield Design**
The tribe do not make regular use of shields. 

## **Battlecry**
A long, sustained “Hissssssssssssssssszzzzzzzzzzzzzz”. 

Common to Savage Orc tribes is use of local bird calls and animal cries for secret communications. 

## Olde Weirde’s Incunabulum
Pfaff dismissed Gronighof’s points. He claimed that Orcs would not utilise crossbows unless instructed on how to (and blamed the irresponsibility of Tilean soldiers of fortune for teaching the Orcs how to operate such weapons), he said the ability to train boars and wyverns was universal, and that the only reason an Orc tribe would not include such creatures would be because of local scarcity, and he flatly denied the possibility that such a thing as an Orc engineer could exist. Gronighof countered that he had seen such a thing as an Orc fortress with his own eyes, but Pfaff insisted that such buildings were no more complex than the crude wooden dwellings of Greenskins, and just scaled up to an admittedly impressive size. 

The Orcs that infest the mountains about the Empire are known for their murderous belligerence and incorrigible manners, and woe betide any scholar who suggests that they might possess the sophistication required to develop an appreciation of culture or mastery of technology. However, they do demonstrate an ability to craft items with wood or steel, though their tools and devices are invariably ugly, crude, and fashioned for no purpose beyond the prosecution of warfare. Innovation seems to be beyond them, they lack the subtlety of thought to operate firearms (to my great relief), and the weapons, armour, and tactics employed by their forces seem to be much the same in the modern era as they were in the time of Sigmar. 

It seemed that Pfaff’s insistence that Orcs possess a universal appreciation of limited technology, no more and no less than has been since their earliest history, was an unassailable hypothesis, and Gronighof appeared to fall into something of a dudgeon due to his inability to undermine the confidence of his rival. I did feel sorry for Gronighof, for to knock a fellow academic off of his high horse is a supreme pleasure for any serious scholar. 

Professor Pfaff posited once in a discussion with Professor Gronighof and myself that Orcs possessed an instinctual understanding of basic carpentry and blacksmithing but lacked the ability to learn beyond the skills necessary to construct items such as cleavers, spears, bows, shields, and suits of armour, and that some limitation of imagination or patience prevented them from developing techniques necessary to think new ideas. This is by no means a controversial opinion, but Pfaff went further in insisting that the perfidious Greenskins possessed a universal ability to craft simple wargear to the standard commonly demonstrated by their fighting forces but were able to think up nothing else. By his account the entire species knew without being taught how to forge weapons and armour but could only comprehend what they knew on instinct and nothing else. 

But just as Pfaff’s resulting aura of smugness grew pungent enough to induce a migraine, Gronighof rallied, and pointed to the existence of those Orc tribes who displayed an aversion to working metal, opting instead to employ weaponry and accoutrements constructed purely from wood, bone, and flint. 

I had heard tell of such Orcs myself, having once spent an evening interrogating a Wastelander sailor who had encountered such a tribe after a shipwreck left him and several shipmates stranded on an island off the east coast of Lustria. 

Professor Gronighof, who is more widely travelled than Pfaff or myself, was more sceptical. He claimed that during a journey through the Border Princes, he learned of a band of Orc mercenaries who had mastered the crossbow (a weapon I have never previously heard of them employing), mentioned their proven track record of training war beasts such as great boars and wyverns (both brutish creatures considered too truculent and unbiddable to be domesticated), and recounted an old story of an Orcish engineer who constructed his own design of mangonel. 

He had said it was an idyllic beach, the weather was pleasant enough in the shade, a babbling stream emptied into a lagoon, where fish swam, and surely the jungle would offer up sufficient food. The marooned sailors made a rudimentary shelter from whatever wreckage had washed up on the beach and decided their time on the island need not be unpleasant. 

design of mangonel.

Except they were not to know that that was the day before the monsoon, a storm that would not let up for weeks. By the third day, they had gone through all the supplies. A band of their gunners had gone hunting, but the birds had nearly all fled and when they finally got a good shot, the black powder fizzled. They set about building a raft from the bits of the ship they scavenged along the shore, but no sooner was it constructed than it was whisked away by the tempest. 

And when things could not get much worse, they were invaded. A tribe of Orcs had been living on the other end of the island, and the sailors’ expeditions had attracted their attention. Two dozen of the green-skinned creatures rushed from the jungle hollering war cries and brandishing spears. They did not possess any armour to speak of. They wore no clothes but rawhide loincloths and the odd fur cloak, they were adorned with many coloured feathers and had painted their skin in gaudy colours. They did not wield the heavy cleavers and other great metal blades Orcs are so feared for but had armed themselves with large bone clubs and chunky flint spears. 

The Orcs edged forwards and made strange guttural ululations. It seemed inevitable that the Wastelanders would be massacred, but as if to an unheard order, the ranks parted and an enormous Orc strode forward. I was already aware that it is a common thing among Orcs that their leader should be the biggest member of the group. Whether such creatures warrant high rank is because they are larger or become larger because they possess high rank is an interesting, hotly debated, subject. The Wastelander claimed this vast chieftain was inspecting them with a warning look, as if wondering which of them would step forward to challenge him. 

The sailor sprang into action, drew forth his cutlass, let out a fierce cry, then promptly tripped over his own feet and faceplanted in the sand. The chief stood there a moment, arms aloft, brandishing a huge bone club, then burst into loud, bellowing laughter. And after a few uneasy moments, his tribe joined him in the hysterics. The Wastelanders must have looked so pathetic, demoralised, and bedraggled, I can only conclude their incompetence saved them. Seeing no threat at all from them, and displaying apparent appreciation for slapstick, the Orcs let them live. They sniffed around menacingly and rooted through the salvaged possessions. One of the Orcs found a prized telescope and whacked another round the head with it, to see if it was any use as a weapon. Disappointed, the creature tossed it to the sand. But the chief picked it up and inspected the apparatus. 

After a few moments of confusion, the sailor stepped forward to demonstrate and showed the Orc chief how to put it to his eye. The creature was delighted with the object, letting out excited hollers. He then became interested in the sailor’s salvaged chest. He rummaged around and discovered a sunstone, a neat artefact used to see the sun on overcast days. The huffing brute was transfixed by the specks of light within. By the end of the day, the Orc chieftain had taken practically everything useful the Wastelanders had managed to save from the wreckage and the Orcs departed with their plunder. 

A few days later, the sailors spotted a passing carrack on its way to Skeggi, and setting fire to their remaining gear, they managed to attract its attention. Five of their number had disappeared during their stay on the island, perhaps having gotten lost or expired due to some mishap whilst foraging. The Wastelander did not mention the Orcs, but I suspect they may well have regarded the Humans on the beach as a handy source of food in lean times, and that it was a desire for fresh flesh that saved the survivors rather than generosity on behalf of the Orcs. 

Pfaff dismissed my tale as hard evidence against his position, claiming that the scarcity of resources on the island explained the eccentricities displayed by the Orcs. However, since that day I have made a study of accounts of Orc tribes who adopt such a lifestyle, and whilst it is true that they seem concentrated in Lustria and the Southlands, some of them make their territories in temperate lands where iron is easily acquired. Even the mountains that surround the Empire are said to be the home of such tribes, and therefore a universal appreciation of technology was not common to all Orcs. 

Pfaff sneered and claimed that his point was that Orcs could not innovate beyond a certain level and that the existence of tribes who failed to attain even the mediocre degree of technological aptitude displayed by most Orcs hardly proved him wrong. This was merely an attempt to retain his dignity however, as both Gronighof and I remembered quite clearly that his earlier remark had been to claim that all Orcs possessed a certain minimal understanding of technological practices and that the example of savage tribes proved him in incontrovertible error. 

Pfaff was so put out he went to bed early and Gronighof and I took to the Street of a Hundred Taverns to celebrate, though Gronighof reacted badly to his second jigger of schnapps, vomited on the boots of a dock worker, and was subjected to a thorough pasting. 

## **Tactics**
The Stone Snake Orcs are engaged in a guerrilla war against the Chaos Dwarfs and their allies. They are not a numerous tribe and hold back from taking risks. Despite the Orcish desire for total Waaagh!, Hizsss Snakeskin keeps them on a very tight leash. However, Hizsss knows his people, and carefully manages their inclinations, finding opportunities for the Soldiers and Elites to go in hard and do serious damage, for the Skirmishers to do their sneaky stuff, and for the more pastorally inclined to farm snakes and mushrooms. They also keep on the move, as described in Disposition of the Stone Snakes. 

Skirmishers are primarily used as scouts and spies, alone or in groups of no more than three. They track and map Chaos Dwarf operations. They even sneak into enemy encampments at night to observe, listen, and gain information for Hizsss. When the tribe travels, they scout ahead for danger and keep the disparate groups informed. 

Proper attacks on travelling Chaos Dwarfs and their caravans involves anything from half a dozen skirmishers to a score of skirmishers and a similar number of elites and soldiers. The Stone Snakes aim either to significantly outnumber the enemy, attack from ambush, or prepare traps. For example, having learnt of a path regularly used by Hobgoblin allies driving coal wagons, the Orcs find a spot that disadvantages the foe, such as a gully or canyon, then dig and disguise potholes or trenches to catch wagon wheels or the legs of draught animals. 

Dropping boulders from cliffs or goading Giant Snakes to attack allows the Orcs to keep their distance until an opportune moment to send in the troops. With regard to Chaos Dwarfs and their allies, Stone Snakes have a no survivors policy, in order to keep themselves a mystery. However, as they help more captives of the Chaos Dwarfs to escape, rumours are emerging. 

## **Rain of Stones**
## **Easy Encounter**
It’s not all Waaagh! Waaagh! Waaagh! with the Stone Snakes. Sometimes they need to eat, too. This encounter involves six to eight ordinary Savage Orcs, perhaps with a single Soldier or Skirmisher keeping watch. If the Characters are numerous or tough, make more Orcs Skirmishers and Soldiers. They are happily minding their own business, combing through the blackened rubble of a fertile escarpment, gathering edible toadstools and deeprooted succulents. 

An **Opposed Perception** Test between the Characters and the most perceptive Orc is required to see which group spots the other first. If the Orcs spot the Characters, they don’t take risks with an obviously strong party. They spread themselves as quickly as possible so they don’t present a single target, ducking for cover, hiding among the rocks. Like snakes, they’re unlikely to attack unless provoked. If they do resort with violence, it’s with slings or thrown rocks. They move, then attack, then move. They’re not especially interested in killing the Characters, but try to drive them away. If they get them running, they’re happy to see them go. They only maintain their barrage if they can strike from cover – Characters entering open land are let go. 

If the Characters spot the Orcs first, what happens depends on the Characters. If they flagrantly attack or threaten the Orcs, they scatter and matters proceed as described above, though the Orcs become more bloodthirsty. The Orcs only enter melee if they’re cornered and have no choice, or if the Characters attack first and the scattered Orcs make first kill. 

However, if the Characters can signal peaceful intentions very quickly – careful diplomacy, slow movements, laying down weapons, offering gifts – the Stone Snakes are cautiously interested.  The Orcs trade food, information about mutual enemies, local dangers, and surrounding lands, but rudely reject any item made of metal. 

The foragers consists of: 

- Six basic Savage Orcs. 

- One Arrer Boy (Skirmisher) with an arrow nocked, in cover. 

## **A Fireside Chat? Medium Encounter**
The Dark Lands experience many strange, dangerous events, including devastating thunder storms. The Characters are caught in one of these. As lightning strikes the ground around them, let them find shelter under a rocky overhang, only to have lightning shatter it. They’re not hurt, but need a safer refuge. Nearby, shelter beckons in the form of a cave entrance. 

If the Characters take this option, they find themselves in the dark. Let them catch their breath. Let them create some illumination. Let them discover they’re sharing a cramped space with a load of Savage Orcs at the back of the cave who are all watching them curiously. 

The Characters are outnumbered, but perhaps not overwhelmed. The number of Soldiers and Elites should make a fight a risky proposition. If the Characters have magic or are very experienced, consider having Hizsss or Slith present. Everyone is hampered by the confines of the cave: ranged weapons are impractical and swords are impossible to swing effectively. If it comes to a fight, it’ll likely be a brawl or a knife fight. Either that, or flee into the earth-shattering lightning. 

In case anyone wonders, the Orcs are not intimidated by fire. They just haven’t made one because they don’t mind the dark and aren’t feeling the cold. If the Characters pull weapons, but don’t attack, the Orcs mirror them. There’s a still a chance to pull back from the brink at this point. If the Characters attack, so do the Orcs. If the fire gets put out in the ruckus, the Characters could be in trouble. 

There are ways out of this: put away weapons; show empty hands; or just peacefully sit down as though everything is cool. The Orcs take or follow the lead depending on the Character’s behaviour. Depending on Characters’ mission in the Dark Lands, this could a productive meeting. 

The fireside chat consists of: 

- Hizsss Snakeskin or Ffang Snake-Wrangla. 

- A bodyguard of two Savage Orc Elites. 

- Six Savage Orc Soldiers. 

## **Wrong Place, Wrong Time Hard Encounter**
The Disposition of the Stone Snakes describes the nomadic tribe’s travel routine. This encounter shows how a party of incautious Characters – or a group with murderous tendencies – can fall foul of that. 

The Characters encounter a small party of Stone Snakes, which they clearly outmatch. The Orcs are foraging, setting-up camp, or sat down roasting a big rat-thing above a fire. If the Characters attack, they’re going to win. If the Characters blindly go in for the kill, fine. When only one is Orc left, or as the last one dies, the Characters are attacked from behind by another group. This one only has one more Orc than the last group. Unless the Characters have been unlucky with the first group, this one doesn’t look challenging either. However, this is the point when the Characters should reevaluate their position. 

If they decide to flee, let them do so, with perhaps some ranged harassment as described in the Easy Encounter: Rain of Stones. The Orcs eventually relent, although the Characters might find themselves stalked and observed for several days. If they continue to fight, the Characters find more and increasingly larger, tougher groups of Orcs appear every couple of rounds. The longer the Characters keep fighting, the harder it becomes to disengage and flee, until they are completely surrounded. 

This is clearly a scenario where all the Characters could legitimately die. However, if the Characters surrender, the Orcs relent. If they don’t, then Hizsss orders the Orcs to take the Characters alive. It’s hard to tell if the Orcs are impressed by their belligerence, wish to punish them, or both. The Orcs were gathering prior to entering a cave system to lure out a particularly monstrous snake. The Characters may now be given the honour of taking point. 

## Campaign Seed
Whilst the Stone Snakes have an unusual perspective for Orcs due to Hizsss’s overriding sense of mission, they are still Orcs, still belligerent, still liable to squabble if bored or poorly led. They also have their tribal territory in the lee of the World’s Edge Mountains, where many Dwarf holds have suffered greatly from the depredations of Orcs. Dwarfs do not forgive their grudges, even in situations where one of their enemies is focused on another. Should the Stone Snakes’ presence become known to the Dwarfs, they will make war upon them, even if the Stone Snakes seek vengeance of their own against the Chaos Dwarfs. 

## **Hizsss Snakeskin – Savage Orc Shaman Lord**
Hizsss was an apprentice without a master when Mork struck him with lightning. The lightning provided him with power, but aged him greatly. Although surprisingly tough and spritely, he looks every bit the elderly Shaman Lord he became. It’s a price he is happy to pay. 

Taking leadership of the tribe from the increasingly eccentric Slith Snake-Wrangla was easy after leading the tribe’s escape from the Chaos Dwarfs. Less easy was encouraging them to adopt a war of stealth against the Chaos Dwarfs: some of the tribe wanted a full-on Waaagh! against them, while others wanted to slink off, live in caves, and farm mushrooms. Hizsss’s middle-way (and threatening language) swung the argument. 

Mork whispers loudly in his ear that he’s doing a good job, monitoring Chaos Dwarf activity and disrupting it wherever possible. Gork’s whispers are quieter, he insists that the Stone Snakes should be “’Eadbuttin’ evvyfing!”

## **Slith Snake-Wrangla – Savage Orc Warlord**
By rights, Slith Snake-Wrangla should be the leader of not just the Stone Snakes, but many neighbouring tribes. However, he has been bitten by so many snakes he’s become somewhat addled from all the venom. 

While this big, muscley Orc hasn’t lost any of his fighting skills, his desire to lead has evaporated. While not quite subservient to Hizsss Snakeskin, he seems content to offer random advice, often unprompted, to anyone needing it, including outsiders. It’s usually good advice too. 

Slith is absolutely covered with scars from fang bites, old and new, easily seen as he wears only a leather kilt. He spends his days catching smaller snakes to milk for venom, and giant ones for skins and meat. He makes a point of strangling giant snakes with his bare hands, saying it’s more respectful. He carries a bagful of pet snakes in a sack he loves to show off.

## **Bruug – Savage Orc Skirmisher**
Though small for an Orc, Bruug is strong and wiry. He wears a dusty, stained snakeskin jerkin, ragged along the edges. He wears a snakeskin patch over one eye (he’s not blind, just thinks it makes him look dangerous). He loves acting as a distraction, scrambling across the rock-strewn landscape, leaping across the crags. Whether drawing the foe into an ambush or leading them away from the rest of the tribe, Bruug relishes the risk. 

He spends much of his time gathering information about Chaos Dwarf movements, tracking supply routes, mining operations and workshops, and observing their interactions with other Orcs, Goblins, and creatures of the Dark Lands. He runs a team of sneaky Orcs, drawing chalk maps on dark slates. 

Bruug is especially proud of the name Hizsss gave him for his bravery in approaching the Ungols the night of the tribe’s initial escape. ‘Ammer Givva’ is an unusual title for an Orc, but it provides Bruug with a deal of self-worth.

## **Garn – Savage Orc Skirmisher**
The arts of spy and assassin are not commonly practised by Orcs, but Garn employs them with a degree of skill. He prefers fighting from a distance, with sling and throwing daggers. He’ll leave close combat to the thugz (Soldiers) and big thugz (Elites). If he must get close, he’ll find ways to strike from behind, above, or below. He gets a thrill using slingshot and remaining unseen, leaving enemies paranoid and confused about what’s hitting them. He spends his spare time milking snakes for venom, priding himself that he’s never been bitten. 

Garn is one of a few Stone Snakes who hold reservations about the arrangement of having a Shaman leading them, instead of a big, ‘ard thug like Slith Snake-Wrangler. Nevertheless, Garn obeys Hizsss, “Coz ‘e’s ded scary!” 

He also secretly admires Bruug but is envious because Hizsss gave him a distinctive name, though Garn would have difficulty articulating such feelings. However, despite these misgivings he is loyal enough to Hizsss, for now.
